name: Helsing
description: Helsing is privately held and has no ticker. Review its funding rounds and valuations, its investors, and the points to confirm before buying or selling.
ledes: Helsing is a privately held defense technology company. Its shares are not listed on an exchange and have no quoted market price; the principal public reference points are the valuations at which the company has raised capital. Its most recent financing, a $1.8 billion Series E round announced on July 13, 2026, valued the company at $18 billion.

Founded in 2021 and based in Munich, Helsing develops artificial intelligence software and autonomous systems for armed forces, including the HX-2 strike drone. Existing shares change hands in privately negotiated transactions and remain subject to the company's transfer restrictions.
table_note: Figures are in U.S. dollars; Helsing announced its rounds before the Series E in euros. The Series E valuation is as announced by the company; the earlier valuations are as reported in the press at the time, and Helsing did not disclose them.
round_notes: Helsing did not name a lead investor for the Series E. The company said that it remained predominantly European-owned after the round.

A round valuation reflects the terms of the preferred stock issued in that round. Most shares sold by employees are common stock, which carries fewer rights and typically trades at a discount to the preferred price.
investors: Investors in the Series E included Dragoneer Investment Group, Iconiq, Lightspeed Venture Partners, the growth equity business of Goldman Sachs Alternatives, JPMorganChase and CPP Investments. Prima Materia, the investment firm of Spotify co-founder Daniel Ek, led the Series D and the Series A, and General Catalyst led the Series C and the Series B. Other investors include Accel, Greenoaks, Saab and BDT & MSD Partners.
spv_sentence: No special purpose vehicles naming Helsing appear in SEC Form D filings.
sources: Sources: Helsing's Series E announcement, as reported by Tech.eu and Defense News (July 13, 2026); a Tech.eu report on the Series D (June 2025), citing the Financial Times; TechCrunch reports dated July 11, 2024 and September 14, 2023; reporting by Bloomberg (July 2024 and July 2026); and SEC Form D filings.
